headline: The admin user screen can now change roles and permanently delete users without visible access controls.
what_changed: The user-management screen now lets staff change a person's role.
The screen now lets staff delete a person after a confirmation message.
The app now accepts requests to change roles or delete users at a new web address.

risks.title: Anyone may control user accounts
risks.explanation: The new web address changes roles and deletes accounts, but it contains no check that the caller is signed in or is an administrator. A person could send requests to it directly, without using the admin screen. They could make themselves an administrator or delete other users, causing loss of access and user data. Add and verify a server-side administrator check before either action.

questions_for_developer: Is there a site-wide access rule that protects this new web address, including direct requests from people who do not use the admin screen? Please show where it is enforced.
When a user is deleted, does the database reliably delete their shifts as the confirmation message promises, or could the deletion fail because shifts still exist?
good_news: The confirmation message reduces accidental deletions from the admin screen.
